_meta.indication: PAR-1 antagonist indicated for the reduction of thrombotic cardiovascular events in patients with a history of myocardial infarction (MI) or with peripheral arterial disease (PAD); shown to reduce the rate of a combined endpoint of cardiovascular death, MI, stroke, and urgent coronary revascularization

pivotal_trials.trial_name: TRA 2°P-TIMI 50 (Thrombin-Receptor Antagonist in Secondary Prevention of Atherothrombotic Ischemic Events)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Large, international, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, parallel group, placebo-controlled cardiovascular outcomes trial; vorapaxar 2.5 mg daily added to standard of care vs. placebo
pivotal_trials.population: 26,449 subjects with a history of myocardial infarction, prior ischemic stroke, or peripheral arterial disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite of cardiovascular (CV) death, MI, stroke, and urgent coronary revascularization (UCR); key secondary endpoint CV death, MI, or stroke
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint: 1417 (10.7%) placebo vs 1259 (9.5%) vorapaxar; HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.82-0.95), p=0.001. Key secondary endpoint (CV death, MI, stroke): HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.80-0.94), p<0.001

key_safety: Increased bleeding risk: in post-MI or PAD patients without stroke/TIA history, GUSTO moderate or severe bleeding 199 (2.0%) placebo vs 303 (3.0%) vorapaxar, HR 1.55 (95% CI 1.30-1.86); any GUSTO bleeding 17.6% vs 25.0%, HR 1.52. Most common non-bleeding adverse reaction: anemia 982 (5.0%) vorapaxar vs 783 (4.0%) placebo
target_moa: Vorapaxar is a reversible antagonist of the protease-activated receptor-1 (PAR-1) expressed on platelets; it inhibits thrombin-induced and thrombin receptor agonist peptide (TRAP)-induced platelet aggregation
modality: Small molecule (tricyclic himbacine-derived selective PAR-1 inhibitor)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: BLEEDING RISK — Do not use in patients with a history of stroke, TIA, or intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), or active pathological bleeding; antiplatelet agents, including ZONTIVITY, increase the risk of bleeding, including ICH and fatal bleeding

rems.type: FDA determined that, at this time, a REMS is not necessary for ZONTIVITY to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks

advisory_committee.vote: Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee (CRDAC) met January 15, 2014 and voted 10 to 1 for approval

basis.text: The review classification for this application is Standard

citations.quote: The review classification for this application is Standard.

summary.text: Standard review of a 505(b)(1) NDA for a new molecular entity (NME); not an accelerated approval. Approval based on the positive Phase 3 TRA 2°P-TIMI 50 outcomes trial; the Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee voted 10 to 1 for approval, and no REMS was required.

citations.quote: The review classification for this application is Standard.

Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated May 10, 2013, received May 10, 2013, submitted under section 505(b)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for ZONTIVITY (vorapaxar) Tablets.
The committee voted 10 to 1 for approval.
We have determined that, at this time, a REMS is not necessary for ZONTIVITY to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks.
